findings.title: Google Meet fallback crashes when destinationCalendar is empty or absent
findings.body: In EventManager.create, evt.destinationCalendar is destructured with `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, which yields undefined when the array is empty or missing, but the next condition dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. For a Google Meet booking with no destination calendar this throws a TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video, breaking booking creation.

findings.title: Google updateEvent fallback cannot find the destination calendar
findings.body: In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent, when externalCalendarId is falsy the fallback searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, comparing calendar IDs to the same falsy value that triggered the fallback, so selectedCalendar is always undefined. calendar.events.update is then called with calendarId undefined and fails, whereas the previous code used the event's destination calendar externalId.

findings.title: Google createEvent uses main host organizer email for every host calendar
findings.body: In GoogleCalendarService.createEvent, selectedCalendar is correctly chosen by matching credentialId, but the payload organizer email still comes from mainHostDestinationCalendar, the first destinationCalendar entry, for every credential. When EventManager creates the event on a second collective host's Google calendar, that event is created with the main host's calendar/externalId as organizer email, which does not match the authenticated host and can produce a wrong organizer or rejected/misattributed event.

findings.title: Office365 createEvent ignores credential-specific destination calendar
findings.body: Office365CalendarService.createEvent always uses the first entry of event.destinationCalendar as mainHostDestinationCalendar and does not accept or use the credentialId now passed by CalendarManager. For collective events, EventManager calls this once per host credential, so a second Office365 host's event is attempted against the main host's calendar externalId with the second host's token, causing failures or an event targeted at the wrong calendar.

findings.title: Lark createEvent always targets the first destination calendar
findings.body: LarkCalendarService.createEvent derives calendarId only from the first destinationCalendar entry and does not use the credentialId supplied for the new multi-destination flow. When EventManager loops over collective hosts and invokes Lark for another host, it will reuse the main host's Lark calendar ID with that host's credentials, so creation fails or targets the wrong calendar instead of that host's destination calendar.

findings.title: CalDAV createEvent can silently create no event for non-main hosts
findings.body: BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters the credential's calendars to those matching mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId, always the first destination calendar. For a second collective host using CalDAV, that externalId is a calendar URL from the main host's server and normally matches none of this host's calendars; the Promise.all then resolves over an empty list and the method returns a generated uid as success even though no calendar object was created, leaving a booking reference pointing to a nonexistent event.

findings.title: updateAllCalendarEvents can reuse the previous reference's credential
findings.body: In EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents, `credential` is declared outside the loop over calendar references. If a later reference's credential is not in calendarCredentials and the DB lookup does not produce a credential, the variable still holds the previous iteration's credential, and updateEvent is pushed with that wrong credential. That can update the previous host's calendar again and leave the intended host's event unchanged.

findings.title: Video booking references lose their credentialId on creation
findings.body: In EventManager.create, referencesToCreate now sets `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so non-calendar results such as video meetings always get credentialId undefined. Previously video results preserved result.credentialId. Later cancellation and update flows look up the video credential by booking reference credentialId, so losing it can prevent the video meeting from being updated or deleted.

findings.title: updateLocation creates calendar references without externalCalendarId or credentialId
findings.body: In EventManager.updateLocation, references are built from result.externalId and result.credentialId, but CalendarManager.updateEvent does not return externalId or credentialId in its EventResult. Calendar references created after a location change therefore lose both identifiers, weakening later update/cancel operations that rely on reference.credentialId and reference.externalCalendarId to target the correct calendar.

findings.title: Recurring collective cancellation repeatedly deletes only the first calendar reference
findings.body: In handleCancelBooking's recurring/allRemainingBookings path, the code now loops over every calendar reference of the booking, but inside that loop it again iterates credentials and for each updated booking selects only `updBooking.references.find(ref => ref.type.includes('_calendar'))`, the first calendar reference. With multiple collective hosts this deletes the first host's recurring events repeatedly and never deletes the other hosts' calendar events, leaving orphaned events after cancellation.

findings.title: Collective team destination calendars are dropped when organizer has none
findings.body: In handleNewBooking, evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists, and the collective handling later does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. If only non-organizer collective hosts have destination calendars, teamDestinationCalendars is collected but never added because the optional-chained push is a no-op on null, so those hosts receive no calendar events.

findings.title: Confirming a collective booking only creates the organizer's calendar event
findings.body: confirmHandler builds evt.destinationCalendar from only booking.destinationCalendar or the confirming user's destinationCalendar, converted to a one-element array. For collective bookings that require confirmation, calendar events are created at confirmation time via this evt, so the other fixed hosts' destination calendars are never passed to EventManager and those hosts do not get calendar events when the booking is confirmed.
